title: Sepher Yetzirah
author: W. Wynn Westcott (trans)
description: Sepher Yetzirah (The Book of Formation and the Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom), translated from the Hebrew with annotations by W. Wynn Westcott (first published 1887; later editions 1893 and 1911), the Freemason and co-founder of the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn. The Sefer Yetzirah, perhaps composed between the second and sixth centuries CE, is the oldest surviving text of Jewish esoteric cosmology. In a few terse chapters it describes how God created the world through the thirty-two paths of wisdom: the ten sefirot ('numbers' or 'spheres') and the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet, divided into three mothers (Aleph, Mem, Shin), seven doubles and twelve simples, corresponding to elements, planets, days, zodiac signs and parts of the body. Westcott adds notes and the Thirty-Two Paths of Wisdom attributed to it. His version shaped the Golden Dawn's attribution of Hebrew letters and Tarot to the Tree of Life.
